flow.costOfRevenueNote: What it cost to run the cloud platform and deliver services — hosting, support and implementation.
flow.grossProfitNote: Revenue left after the direct cost of running the platform — 77.5% of revenue, down from 79.0% a year ago.
flow.netIncomeNote: The bottom line: $385M kept as profit, 12.0% of revenue — GAAP profit is small because $499M of stock-based pay sits inside the costs above.
flow.operatingIncomeNote: An $358M operating profit — an 11.1% margin, up from $240M a year ago. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based pay and other items, it was $955M.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big enterprises — the largest running cost, up from $960M a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the AI platform, including Now Assist and agentic AI; up from $643M a year ago.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day; up from $232M a year ago.

flow.otherIncomeNote: $116M of interest income on the cash pile, less $3M of other expense.
flow.revenueNote: Money from software subscriptions and professional services.
flow.taxNote: An $86M tax provision on $471M of pre-tax income — an 18.3% effective rate.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent, so the rounded rows sum to the rounded $11.98 of profit per $100. Stock-based compensation of $499M is spread across the cost and expense rows above — it is a real cost to shareholders through dilution, even though no cash leaves the bank.
footerNote: Subscription revenue up 22.5% to $3.11B; net income $385M.

kpis.label: Current remaining performance obligations
kpis.note: +24.5% YoY; revenue contracted for the next 12 months

oneTimers: A $30M impairment of assets in the quarter — a write-down excluded from non-GAAP results; there was none a year ago.
Severance costs of $29M in the quarter, excluded from non-GAAP results; there were none a year ago.

Stock-based compensation of $499M (up from $444M a year ago) is the largest non-GAAP add-back and the main reason GAAP operating income of $358M trails non-GAAP operating income of $955M. It is excluded from non-GAAP results, but it is a real cost — it dilutes existing shareholders.
otherDetail: Other income of $113M is $116M of interest income on ServiceNow's cash and investments, less $3M of other expense, net.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: The AI platform, sold by subscription — 97% of all revenue; up 22.5% YoY. Subscription gross profit was $2,488M, an 80% margin.

segments.name: Professional services & other
segments.note: Implementation and consulting help for customers; up 19.5% YoY. Gross profit was just $3M — this work is nearly break-even by design.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Jun 30, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Subscription revenue grew 22.5% to $3.11B — 97% of all revenue — with 89 deals over $1M in net new annual contract value in the quarter. The customer base keeps moving upmarket: 528 customers now spend more than $5M a year, up about 19.5%, and customers over $20M grew more than 30%.
takeaways.title: Subscriptions did the growing

takeaways.text: Current remaining performance obligations — revenue already contracted for the next 12 months — grew 24.5% to $10.92B, and total remaining obligations reached $23.9B, up 29%. The contracted backlog is growing faster than revenue, which is what funds the next quarters.
takeaways.title: The backlog is growing faster than sales

takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was just $358M, an 11.1% margin, while non-GAAP operating income was $955M at a 29.5% margin. The $597M gap is mostly $499M of stock-based pay, plus a $30M asset impairment and $29M of severance. Free cash flow was $535M, a 16.5% margin, and ServiceNow bought back $361M of its own stock.
takeaways.title: The GAAP profit is a third of the adjusted one

verdict: ServiceNow grew revenue 22.5% to $3.22 billion, with subscription sales up 22.5% and $10.9 billion of revenue already contracted for the next twelve months.
